title: Engineering Estimating Standard: Construction Cost, Allowance and Contribution — Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
The staking engineer's estimate on a **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** project at Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative states the construction cost with loading, the allowance applied and the contribution the member must pay, together with the overhead feet, the underground feet, whether the line is three-phase and the transformer capacity to be installed. When it is issued the project moves from engineering to estimate issued status. The three amounts are defined as follows, each figure being the one the class of extension sets.

## 1. Construction cost

The construction cost is the total of:

1. the overhead feet at the class's per-foot overhead cost for the phase built (single-phase or three-phase);
2. the underground feet at the class's per-foot underground cost for the phase built;
3. the charge per kVA for each kVA of transformer capacity above the capacity included in the line cost;
4. the road bore charge for each road or driveway bore;
5. the right-of-way clearing charge for each foot of overhead line;
6. the frost surcharge for each foot of underground line trenched in the frost months;

that total being increased by the engineering and overhead loading percent, and the loaded amount rounded to the cent. The loading acts once, on the whole of items 1 through 6. The per-foot costs are the single-phase overhead, single-phase underground, three-phase overhead and three-phase underground figures, chosen for the line type and phase actually built. Underground construction is required where the class is built underground only.

## 2. Allowance

| Allowance basis of the class | Allowance |
|---|---|
| Footage | The free footage allowance multiplied by the per-foot overhead cost of the phase built |
| Revenue multiple | The revenue multiple allowance multiplied by the estimated annual revenue |
| None | Zero |

The allowance never exceeds the construction cost: where the figure above is larger than the cost, the allowance is the cost.

## 3. Contribution

The contribution is the construction cost less the allowance, less the member trenching credit for each foot the member trenches, and never below zero. On a Temporary Construction Service the temporary service fee is billed instead.

## Worked examples (hypothetical projects, at the class figures in force)

**A. Permanent Residential Overhead Extension, 240 ft single-phase overhead, 25 kVA transformer, no bores.**
Line 240 ft at $14.75, $3,540.00; clearing 240 ft at $2.10, $504.00; no transformer charge, 25 kVA not exceeding the included 25 kVA. Total $4,044.00, increased by 12.5 percent: construction cost $4,549.50. Allowance 300 ft at $14.75, $4,425.00. Contribution $4,549.50 less $4,425.00: **$124.50**.

**B. The same class, 200 ft.** Line $2,950.00, clearing $420.00, total $3,370.00, loaded cost $3,791.25. The footage figure of $4,425.00 is larger than the cost, so the allowance is $3,791.25 and the contribution is **$0.00**.

**C. Permanent Residential Underground Extension, 400 ft single-phase underground trenched in January, one road bore, 25 kVA, of which the member trenches 100 ft.**
Line 400 ft at $22.40, $8,960.00; frost surcharge 400 ft at $5.00, $2,000.00; bore $950.00; no clearing on underground line. Total $11,910.00, loaded cost $13,398.75. Allowance 150 ft at the single-phase overhead cost of $14.75, $2,212.50. Trenching credit 100 ft at $4.50, $450.00. Contribution $13,398.75 less $2,212.50, less $450.00: **$10,736.25**.

**D. Three-Phase Commercial Extension, 2,000 ft three-phase overhead, 150 kVA, estimated annual revenue $9,000.00.**
Line 2,000 ft at $31.80, $63,600.00; transformer 150 kVA above the included 0 kVA at $48, $7,200.00; clearing 2,000 ft at $2.10, $4,200.00. Total $75,000.00, loaded cost $84,375.00. Allowance 3.0 times $9,000.00, $27,000.00. Contribution **$57,375.00**.
